# PowerPlay v2.1.0 — Fire TV

*Plex-focused Fire TV app · Fire OS 7/8 · ARMv7*

## Changes in this release

- Add **experimental Pro Logic I-compatible matrix surround** for receivers that decode original Dolby Pro Logic. The setting is **disabled by default** under **Settings → Video Playback → Audio**.
- Keep playback on **ExoPlayer/Media3**. When enabled, multichannel audio decoded to PCM is converted in real time into a two-channel Lt/Rt matrix; center is phase-compatible and the combined mono surround uses a band-limited quadrature signal. No additional device, server transcode, or file conversion is required.
- Preserve existing **two-channel stereo and pre-encoded Dolby Surround stereo** rather than matrix-encoding them again. Mono is routed equally to both output channels. Source layouts from 3.0 through 7.1 are handled, with surrounds combined into one mono rear channel; discrete LFE is not recreated.
- Add **Speaker diagnostics → Test Pro Logic speaker output** in Video Playback settings. Play individual front-left, center, front-right, and mono rear-surround test tones to verify speaker steering through the Fire TV → HDMI → optical PCM → stereo DAC → legacy receiver signal path. Testing works with the playback preference disabled.
- Keep existing PowerPlay 2.0.2 branding, icon selections, PowerLink/PowerShuffle playback and queue-handoff behavior, Home Assistant compatibility, application identity, saved settings, and Fire TV update route. No intentional dependency changes.

## Compatibility and testing

This is an **experimental, opt-in surround feature**, not a licensed or certified Dolby encoder. Original Pro Logic reconstructs front left, center, front right and a *shared mono rear* from two PCM channels; it does not restore discrete 5.1 or a discrete LFE channel.

Use stereo PCM output on Fire TV and your TV, disable TV sound enhancements where possible, and select Dolby Pro Logic on the receiver. Always test at a modest volume. Speaker steering, channel phase preservation, and performance on individual Fire TV/TV/DAC/receiver combinations require real-device verification. Standard playback behavior remains the default until the option is explicitly enabled.
